description:
Found by the blind-escape census while doing fz-5xp.8.

Giving `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` an `any`/`any` clause -- so the operators
themselves carry Erlang's total term order the way Elixir's do -- makes the
seat unable to separate the typed clauses from the fallback wherever an operand
is unresolved:

    compiler2_dispatch_blind_escape_census_is_the_known_population FAILED
    mailbox_closure_enum_hofs.fz callsite 5 (executable 4) subject 0:
      binary is seated before atom | opaque | var | any | any | any | any | any

The callsite is `fn (x) -> x > 1 end` sent through a mailbox, so `x` is
genuinely unresolved. With only typed clauses the callsite resolves; adding a
catch-all widens what the seat admits and it goes blind. Four more pins moved
with it (drive_test permuted-arm invariance, the public-trace claims, the
work-start frontier).

The census is explicit that this is not a re-bless: 'a new entry under ANY
setting is a new latent miscompile and wants a ticket, not a re-blessed
constant.'

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD (fz-5xp.8): the total order is real and reachable through
`Kernel.compare/2`, and `Enum.sort/1` uses it. The operators keep their typed
clauses, so `1 < :atom` is refused at COMPILE time rather than answered wrongly
at run time. fz-5xp.8's description names this as the decision it wanted made,
so it is the ticket's own alternative rather than a cut.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is a dispatch problem rather than a library one: for the
operators to carry the order the way Elixir's do, the seat has to separate a
`binary` clause from an `any` clause on an unresolved subject. That is the
axis work fz-kdt.119 and fz-kdt.107 did for tuples and lists, not something the
runtime library can arrange.

Blocks nothing today -- sorting has its order. Reopen when the seat can read it.
title: A comparison operator with an any/any clause makes every unresolved callsite dispatch-blind
